rows.title: 'We are close,' to deal with Canada, Trump's trade representative says
rows.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Fox News on Sunday that Canada and the United States are fairly close to a trade deal after a lot of progress. Talks had collapsed in August when Ottawa walked away from last-minute U.S. terms, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said included limits on Canada signing trade deals with other countries. Both sides restarted efforts in November after Trump's Republicans did poorly in the U.S. midterm elections, where several Democrats blamed the trade war with Canada for high living costs. Greer said Washington is uneasy about Canada's trade reset with China, especially its decision to let 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles a year into Canada at a lower tariff. Canada's chief negotiator Janice Charette has told a federal advisory committee that several issues remain open, the largest being the 25% U.S. tariff on Canadian cars.
rows.fact: Greer said on Sunday that the U.S. and Canada are close to a deal and are holding constructive talks on managing North American trade in autos, steel and aluminum. He also said Canada's lower tariff on up to 49,000 Chinese EVs a year worries Washington, while Canadian officials say the 25% U.S. tariff on Canadian vehicles is the biggest unresolved issue.
rows.outlook: Greer said both sides are close to finding a landing zone, but Canada's negotiators say multiple trade issues are still unresolved.
rows.why: 관세 전쟁을 끝내려는 협상에서 자동차·철강 같은 핵심 산업과 '중국과의 관계'가 왜 걸림돌이 되는지, 무역 협상이 실제로 어떻게 진행되는지 볼 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a trade war is negotiated toward an end, and why key industries like autos and steel, plus ties with China, become sticking points.
rows.term_def: A tax a country charges on imported goods. It makes foreign products more expensive, which can protect local producers but raises prices for buyers and invites the other country to retaliate.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no new Canadian government/BoC policy confirmed in last 24h; StatCan's Nov. 23 releases were not yet readable). Greer's remarks were made Nov. 22 ET; cross-checked with the National Post report (Swikar Oli) via Yahoo News Canada, which adds that U.S. auto tariffs are set to rise from 25% to 50% in January. Distinct from the already-covered Carney China visit story.

opinion.title: Carney striking trade deals at 'lightning speed' amid diversification push: expert
opinion.author: Jordan Fleguel (interview with Margaret Kim, Gowling WLG)
opinion.summary: International trade lawyer Margaret Kim of Gowling WLG says Canada has been concluding free trade agreements with ASEAN partners and the Philippines very quickly as it tries to rely less on the U.S. amid increasingly complex relations. She calls China's tariff relief on Canadian pork and seafood, in exchange for easing on Chinese steel and aluminum, a positive step, but stresses these are provisional arrangements rather than a full free trade deal that would give businesses certainty. She notes China wants to sell more EVs in Canada and that Carney has said any such move must fit within CUSMA. Kim does not expect CUSMA to disappear but expects different versions of it, and says the face-to-face Carney-Trump meeting at APEC is a good sign for the still-unfinished U.S. talks. The article notes tariffs and counter-tariffs between the two countries remain in place.
opinion.why: 미국 의존도를 줄이려는 캐나다의 '무역 다변화' 전략이 미국과의 협상, 특히 중국 문제와 어떻게 맞물리는지 전문가 시각으로 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: An expert explains how Canada's push to diversify trade away from the U.S. connects to the U.S. talks, including the China question.

rows.title: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, says Farm Bureau survey
rows.summary: The American Farm Bureau Federation's annual survey, which uses volunteer shoppers in all 50 states and Puerto Rico, puts the cost of a Thanksgiving feast for 10 at $58.63, up 6% from last year and the first increase since the 2022 record of $64.05. A big reason is diesel: AAA says the fuel's price has climbed since the Iran war began, hitting a record $6.53 a gallon in September and still averaging $5.96, 58% above a year earlier, which raises the cost of processing and shipping milk, rolls, potatoes and cranberries. A 16-pound turkey rose to $23.68 from $21.50 because growing demand for lean protein and rising exports tightened inventories even as production recovered from bird flu, while a few items such as frozen peas and vegetable trays got slightly cheaper. Retailers like Aldi ($39) and Walmart ($35) are offering cheaper holiday meal bundles to draw shoppers. Government data show food-at-home prices rose 22% from October 2021 to October 2026, roughly double the usual pace, and grocery costs contributed to Republicans' recent midterm losses.
rows.fact: The Farm Bureau estimates a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 costs $58.63 this year, up 6% and the first rise since 2022, with a 16-pound turkey up to $23.68 from $21.50. Diesel prices, up 58% from a year ago since the Iran war began, are raising the cost of processing and transporting many staples.
rows.outlook: The USDA expects wholesale frozen turkey prices to average a record $1.76 a pound (up 29%) and food-at-home prices to rise 2.3% this year, while an analyst says diesel's impact on turkey prices will be more noticeable next year.
rows.why: 전쟁으로 오른 경유값이 운송·가공비를 거쳐 추수감사절 식탁 물가까지 끌어올리는 과정을 통해, 에너지 가격이 경제 전체로 퍼지는 원리를 쉽게 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a war-driven jump in diesel prices travels through shipping and processing costs all the way to a family's holiday dinner, a clear example of how energy prices ripple through the economy.
rows.term_def: The price stores and restaurants pay suppliers when they buy goods in bulk, before adding their own markup. When wholesale prices rise, shoppers usually see higher retail prices soon after.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no major US government/Fed economic announcement in the last 24h, Sunday-Monday US time). Survey released Nov. 18 ET; PBS page timestamp is Nov. 19, 6:30 p.m. EST (Nov. 20 KST). Total, 6% rise and $23.68 turkey cross-checked with the Farm Bureau's own Nov. 18 release and Market Intel analysis.

opinion.title: Why Thanksgiving Prices Are Higher Than Ever.
opinion.author: Errol Schweizer (contributor)
opinion.summary: Food-industry contributor Errol Schweizer argues that this year's pricier Thanksgiving comes from the Iran war, tariffs and big companies raising prices during a crisis. Citing an analysis by the Groundwork Collaborative and The Century Foundation, he says a full Thanksgiving basket costs about 11% more than last year, roughly three times overall inflation, with wholesale frozen turkey up about 30%. He points to war-related jumps in diesel and fertilizer costs that raise animal feed prices, bird flu, 50% tariffs on imported steel and tin plate that make canned goods costlier, and raids on immigrant farmworkers, and notes that five processors control over 60% of turkey sales. He uses economist Isabella Weber's idea of 'sellers inflation' to argue firms with market power raise prices beyond their cost increases, and stresses that food takes a much larger share of income for low earners. He urges Congress to act with measures such as a higher minimum wage, restored SNAP benefits, windfall profit taxes and antitrust enforcement, warning that holiday prices could rise further in 2027.
opinion.why: 같은 '추수감사절 물가'라도 어떤 장바구니로 재느냐에 따라 상승률이 6%에서 11%까지 달라지고, 원인을 비용 상승으로 볼지 기업의 가격 결정력으로 볼지에 따라 해법도 달라진다는 점을 생각해 볼 수 있는 칼럼입니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that the same holiday price rise can measure 6% or 11% depending on the basket used, and that whether you blame rising costs or corporate pricing power changes which policies you'd favor.

rows.title: Gov't prepares market stabilization fund due to sharp downturns in domestic, global stocks
rows.original_source: Korea JoongAng Daily (Ahn Hyo-seong, Jang Seo-yun)
rows.summary: After an emergency meeting on Sunday with the Bank of Korea governor and the heads of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il announced steps to steady South Korea's falling stock market. The government will get a market stabilization fund ready, financed by financial institutions, that could buy index-linked products and other securities to counter sharp drops, although its size and launch date have not been set. For three months starting Tuesday, daily limits on listed companies' share buyback orders will be eased, and regulators will step up surveillance of illegal short selling, margin lending and forced liquidations. The moves came after the Kospi fell 5.21% on Friday and U.S. chip stocks plunged, with officials blaming uncertainty over AI industry profits and financing, U.S. data center rules and tighter chip export controls. A similar 10.76 trillion won fund was set up in 2020 during the pandemic but never used because the market rebounded.
rows.fact: South Korea's financial authorities said they are preparing a stock market stabilization fund, easing companies' daily share buyback limits for three months and tightening monitoring of illegal short selling. The steps followed a 5.21% Kospi drop on Friday and a steep fall in U.S. semiconductor stocks, with the fund's size and timing still undecided.
rows.outlook: Officials said the chip sector's long-term growth prospects remain intact and urged investors not to panic-sell.
rows.why: 주가가 급락할 때 정부와 중앙은행이 어떤 수단(안정기금, 자사주 매입 완화, 공매도 감시)으로 시장의 공포를 누그러뜨리려 하는지 보여주는 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows which tools a government and central bank reach for, such as a rescue fund, looser buyback rules and short-selling checks, to calm panic when stock prices crash.
rows.term_def: Borrowing shares and selling them, hoping to buy them back later at a lower price and keep the difference. It can make price drops bigger in a downturn, so regulators watch it closely in a crash.
rows.note: Government measure announced Sunday Nov. 22 KST after the F4 meeting (roughly 24-36h before edition time; reported Nov. 23). This is the actual policy decision, a follow-up to the Nov. 22 'calls for bolder stabilization measures' item, not a repeat. Measures cross-checked with Korea Herald reports (finance minister press conference; KH Explains piece): fund preparation is not a decision to deploy, no money committed yet.

opinion.title: Can 2008-era tool stop the latest market rout?
opinion.author: Choi Yeon-jae
opinion.summary: This 'KH Explains' piece looks at whether the Securities Market Stabilization Fund can halt the slide, after the Kospi fell another 3.31% to 4,708.54 on Monday and triggered a sell-side sidecar for a second straight session. The fund pools money from state-run banks and major financial groups through a capital call, meaning participants hand over committed money only after regulators activate it. It has been set up five times since 1990 and used in 2003 and 2008, when about 515 billion won was injected; the 2020 fund was never deployed. Samsung Securities research head Yoon Sok-mo argues the fund cannot drive a rally but signals that authorities will defend against further falls, and sees 4,300 as a fairly firm floor, while a Kiwoom Securities researcher warns of 4,200-4,300 in a worst case. Others, including the Korea Institute of Finance, say past effects were limited and the fund might simply absorb foreign selling.
opinion.why: 정책이 실제로 돈을 쓰지 않고도 '신호'만으로 시장 심리에 영향을 줄 수 있는지, 그리고 그 한계는 무엇인지 생각해 볼 수 있는 분석입니다.
opinion.why_en: It helps you think about whether a policy can move markets just by sending a signal, without spending money, and where that approach falls short.

rows.title: Euro zone growth holds steady but France clouds outlook
rows.summary: S&P Global's flash composite PMI for the euro zone held at 51.7 in November, slightly below the 51.9 that economists polled by Reuters expected but above 50 for a fifth straight month, meaning business activity is still growing. S&P Global said the reading points to fourth-quarter growth of close to 0.3%. Behind the steady average, Germany's output grew at its fastest pace since March 2022 on a manufacturing upturn, while France suffered its sharpest contraction in six months, with business sentiment near record lows outside the pandemic as firms and households hold back ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The services PMI fell to a five-month low of 51.2 while the manufacturing PMI rose to 52.9, and services firms cut jobs for a second month. Input costs kept rising sharply but at the slowest rate in three months, and selling-price growth was the weakest since August.
rows.fact: The euro zone composite PMI stayed at 51.7 in November, signalling continued growth consistent with roughly 0.3% expansion in the fourth quarter. Germany's output grew at the fastest rate since March 2022 while France's shrank at the fastest rate in six months, and services slowed to a five-month low as manufacturing improved.
rows.outlook: Business confidence about the year ahead fell for a fourth month to its lowest since May, and S&P Global's Chris Williamson warned that the steady headline hides widening gaps between member countries.
rows.why: 유로존 전체 평균은 안정적이지만 독일과 프랑스가 정반대로 움직이는 모습을 통해, 하나의 통화를 쓰는 나라들 사이에서도 경기 흐름이 얼마나 다를 수 있는지 보여줍니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a steady average can hide very different paths, with Germany booming and France shrinking, even among countries that share one currency.
rows.term_def: A monthly survey asking company managers whether output, orders, jobs and prices are rising or falling. A reading above 50 means activity is growing; below 50 means it is shrinking. Because it comes out before official GDP data, it is watched as an early signal of the economy.
rows.note: Released today (Nov 23) but it is a private S&P Global survey, not an official government/central bank release; no major EU/ECB policy announcement found in the last 24h. Figures cross-checked with AFP report via Free Malaysia Today (51.7 unchanged, ~0.3% Q4 pace; AFP cites FactSet forecast of 52.0, Reuters poll 51.9).

opinion.title: Eurozone growth maintains its pace as France weakens further
opinion.author: Bert Colijn
opinion.summary: ING economist Bert Colijn reads the unchanged 51.7 composite PMI as evidence that the eurozone economy keeps growing at a decent pace. He expects the bloc to end 2026 without a recession, having absorbed the Middle East war and the energy supply shock better than many feared. He stresses the contrast inside the average: France slipped deeper into contraction, while Germany's composite index hit its highest level since 2022 thanks to a perceived surge in manufacturing. Colijn cautions that strong factory surveys have not yet shown up in official industrial production data, which keeps disappointing. He also notes that price pressures eased to a three-month low, suggesting inflation is not speeding up for now.
opinion.why: 설문조사(PMI)가 보여주는 경기와 실제 생산 통계가 어긋날 수 있다는 점을 짚어 주어, 경제 지표를 비판적으로 읽는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It points out that business surveys and hard production data can disagree, teaching you to read economic indicators critically.

rows.title: Chinese exchanges announce measures to aid markets
rows.summary: China's three main stock exchanges in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing announced steps on Sunday to support falling share prices. From November 30, the minimum margin ratio for buying stocks with borrowed money drops to 80% from 100%, so investors can borrow more against the same collateral; this reverses a tightening made in January. The exchanges said margin financing had weakened significantly while overall leverage is low, and Shanghai and Shenzhen also cut trading fees, while Shenzhen proposed a market-making system for its ChiNext startup board to calm price swings. The moves follow earlier November measures by Beijing, as Chinese stocks have been hit by slow domestic growth, a global sell-off in AI shares and geopolitical tension: the Shanghai Composite fell nearly 3% last week to a 16-month low, and the STAR and ChiNext boards are down more than 40% from June peaks. Outstanding margin loans have fallen more than 20% to about 2.2 trillion yuan ($329 billion) from a late-June peak of 3 trillion yuan, and South Korea and Taiwan have also taken steps to steady their markets.
rows.fact: China's Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges will cut the minimum margin ratio for leveraged stock purchases to 80% from 100% from November 30, and Shanghai and Shenzhen will cut trading fees. Margin loans have dropped more than 20% from their June peak to about 2.2 trillion yuan as stocks slid to a 16-month low.
rows.why: 정부가 '빚을 내서 주식을 사는 규칙'을 풀어 주가를 떠받치려 할 때 어떤 효과와 위험이 따르는지, 그리고 AI 주식 급락이 아시아 시장 정책까지 움직이고 있음을 보여 줍니다.
rows.why_en: It shows what happens when authorities loosen the rules on buying stocks with borrowed money to prop up prices, and how the global AI stock sell-off is now driving policy across Asian markets.
rows.term_def: Borrowing money from a broker to buy stocks. The margin ratio is how much of your own money or collateral you must put up; a lower ratio lets you borrow more, which can boost gains but also deepens losses if prices fall.
rows.note: Last-24h policy item (exchanges' notices dated Nov. 22, Reuters published Nov. 22 08:00 EST = 22:00 KST). Reuters text cross-checked on MarketScreener; CSRC approval, ~400 billion yuan freed-up liquidity estimate (industry/Chinese media estimate) and Jan. 2026 tightening confirmed via The Standard (HK) and Trading Economics.

opinion.title: China cuts margin requirement to 80% in fresh market support push, but will it work?
opinion.author: Eamonn Sheridan
opinion.summary: Sheridan explains the margin cut and notes it fulfills a pledge from a larger November 2 package that included central bank swap support for brokers, funds and insurers and cheaper relending for share buybacks. He argues that easier margin rules make borrowing cheaper but do not create demand on their own, because falling loan balances suggest investors are choosing to cut risk rather than being blocked from taking it. He warns that more leverage works both ways: if prices keep falling, margin calls could force selling and deepen the decline. He calls the fee cuts modest next to recent losses and says the bigger test is external, since Chinese tech has been hit by the same AI-driven rout as Wall Street and Seoul. The clearest sign the support is working, he says, would be a steady rise in margin balances after November 30.
opinion.why: 정부가 대출 규칙을 풀어도 투자자가 원하지 않으면 수요가 생기지 않는다는 점, 즉 '공급 측 완화'의 한계를 쉽게 이해할 수 있는 해설입니다.
opinion.why_en: It clearly explains why loosening borrowing rules cannot create demand if investors do not want to take risk, showing the limits of this kind of policy support.
